reply_text:
Loop changes are in; now tightening the citation rule in the pack, then launching.Committing, then launching hour 2.㊥ Gist: The second hour started at about 23:25 UTC with all the improvements, on the same four seats: kimi-3, codex-9, codex-4 and codex-6. Finished packs no longer notify me, so you should not see a notice per pack this time. I will check quality at about 00:30 UTC.

㊢ (what changed, commit 48296e5f)
- **Which turns:**
  - The loop skips turns whose origin was never matched, and turns over 20 sentences. Those are where the harness prompts and the transcript saved three times came from.
  - I built the remaining 19 July blocks. That leaves 812 eligible July turns, more than an hour needs.
- **Citations:** the pack now says the pattern hits are search results, not suggestions, and that sharing words is not a fit. A citation must quote the pattern's IF condition and say how your turn meets it. The pack also gives the expected rate: about one fragment in five.
- **Citation rate:** the loop logs each pack's citation rate and flags any pack over 40%.
- **小象 training:**
  - 小象 now skips unmatched-origin turns, so hour 1's harness text is out of its training and scoring.
  - Its edition on that basis: 3,022 turns, accuracy 0.355, macro F1 0.222.
  - Accuracy fell slightly because the turns it no longer counts include those it found easy.
- **No per-pack notices:** the loop dispatches under the id `xiang-backfill-loop`, which is not on the roster, so Agency sends no bellback. The loop polls each job itself.

㊟ (not in this run) The check of hour 1's citations by a second reader, change 2 of the four, is not running yet. Until it runs, hour 1's citations stay out of the pattern graph. I will dispatch it after this hour, when Kimi is free and hour 2's citation rate shows how much checking is needed.

㊢ (check at the hour) The wake-up is park `park-92d9e4d5-dcd8-4925-856e-8a3bb276b062`, a timer set for about 00:30 UTC. I will report for each seat:
- throughput and refusals;
- whether the citation rate fell;
- three records read in full, one Kimi and two Codex, with every citation checked against its pattern;
- a 小象 edition logged.

Hour 2 has ended. The citation rate fell from 50–97% to about 20%. Now I'm checking a few refusals and reading sample records.㊥ Gist: Hour 2 published about 450 turns, more than hour 1's 340. The tighter rule cut Codex's citation rate from 50–97% to about 20–25%, close to Kimi's. Of the three citations I read in full, two fit their patterns and one was a stretch. I suggest Kimi now checks hour 1's roughly 470 Codex citations.

㊢ (throughput, 23:25–00:25 UTC) The loop is still waiting on its last few jobs.

| Seat | Packs | Turns published | Refused | Minutes per pack | Citation rate per pack |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| codex-4 | 15 | 130 | 12 | 4.0 | 0.05–0.47, mostly about 0.25 |
| codex-6 | 17 | 131 | 2 | 3.8 | 0–0.36, one pack at 1.0 |
| codex-9 | 16 | 140 | 7 | 3.4 | 0–0.47, mostly about 0.25 |
| kimi-3 | 6 | 49 | 0 | 9.8 | 0.04–0.29 |

- **Flags:** 4 packs went over the 40% limit, against nearly all of them in hour 1.
- **Refusals:** most were turns where the record check stopped with an error. All of those were published on retry.
- **Unpublished turns** in the blocks are mainly the ones whose origin could not be matched, which the loop now skips on purpose.

㊬ (three records, each citation checked against its pattern)
- **kimi-3, codex-1-turn-6:** Your "not close it by fiat, but with evidence" is cited as `aif/no-self-certification`. That fits loosely: the pattern is about verdicts that evidence the instrument produced itself can move, and you asked for evidence. Your "run a demonstration loop that you stage as GROUND-CONTROL" is cited as `peripherals/pilot-plus-ground-control`. That is a good fit, because you named the role.
- **codex-9, claude-4-turn-131:** Your "not 'does it have a deposit' but 'is work done'" is cited as `process/fake-done-via-binary-closure`. That is a good fit: the pattern is about an open-or-closed status that stands in for whether the work is done.
- **codex-4, claude-9-turn-2:** Your "it should keep displaying in follow mode, can you fix that directly?" is cited as `peripherals/read-only-first-then-extend`. That does not fit. The pattern says a new peripheral should first only observe, and you were asking for a display bug fix. It is the same kind of word-match error as in hour 1, but now much rarer.

The segments and intents in all three records read correctly.

㊢ (小象 edition 9) 3,493 turns, accuracy 0.357, macro F1 0.224. That is almost unchanged from edition 8, with about 470 more turns.

㊭ (next)
1. **Citation check by Kimi:** give it hour 1's Codex citations, about 470 across 245 turns, in packs of about 25. Each pack sets the cited fragment beside the pattern's IF and conclusion, and Kimi answers keep or drop. Dropped citations are removed from the record, and the fragment then needs a rejection and a candidate. At Kimi's pace this is about two hours on kimi-3 alone. Codex can keep reading new turns meanwhile.
2. **Hour 3:** run the loop again on the same seats; 812 eligible July turns are left, minus the 450 read this hour.
3. **Hour 2's citations:** check them later by sampling, not in full. At this rate most look plausible.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I start the citation check on kimi-3, and run hour 3 on the three Codex seats alongside it?

previous_reply_acts.text:
(what is running) A new script, `scripts/backfill_loop.py` (commit 5ab71a4a), runs as the user unit `xiang-backfill-loop`. Each seat loops through five steps:
1. Claim ten unread turns.
2. Build a pack.
3. Dispatch it.
4. Wait for the job, then publish through the validator.
5. Log one line to `storage/operator-turns/backfill-loop.jsonl`.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (which turns) The loop first takes the 63 turns left in the 1 to 21 August block, then July. The August 22 onwards blocks already have older readings, so the next unread months are July and earlier. I built three July blocks of 100 turns. At about seven minutes a pack, four seats should read 250 to 300 turns this hour, so that is enough.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(limits of this run)
- **No second readings:** the one-in-ten reread is not in this run, so there is no agreement figure yet.
- **Refused turns are only logged,** not sent back to the reader. They come round once more in a later pack.
- **Codex usage:** the weekly window read 84% used this afternoon. Three Codex seats for an hour may hit the limit. Failed jobs would show up in the log as errors, and the Kimi seat would carry on.
